claims.text: The presently used FeCoNiCrAl feedstock has a particle-size range of 15–45 μm and is used for APS deposition.
Cold spraying with substrate preheating to approximately 200 °C will produce an FeCoNiCrAl coating thicker than 100 μm.
The proposed cold-spray process will produce a denser, lower-porosity coating than APS.
The proposed cold-spray process will produce less as-sprayed oxidation than APS.
Substrate preheating will improve coating adhesion.
Cold spraying FeCoNiCrAl at 600–800 °C, approximately 3–5 MPa, and a 20–30 mm standoff distance in argon or helium provides an effective deposition window.
Under the proposed conditions, cold-sprayed particles remain solid and avoid in-flight melting.
High-velocity solid-state impact causes severe particle plastic deformation and adiabatic shear.
Impact-induced plastic deformation and adiabatic shear improve interparticle bonding and coating densification.
Substrate preheating promotes cold welding and metallurgical bonding at the coating–substrate interface.
Substrate preheating reduces the thermal gradient during deposition.
Keeping particle temperatures below melting limits significant oxidation.
Mechanical interlocking of deformed particles contributes to a dense coating.
Conventional APS deposition produces an FeCoNiCrAl bond-coat thickness of 15–45 μm.
APS exposes HEA particles to melting-related transformations and oxidation.
The improved adhesion from preheating will preserve coating integrity during subsequent high-temperature TBC service.
The proposed coating will remain effective during typical high-temperature exposure and thermal cycling if particle-size and inert-atmosphere boundaries are maintained.

contradictions.description: The 15–45 μm range is identified as feedstock particle size in the initial state but is subsequently treated as the APS coating-thickness baseline.

The intervention changes both the deposition method and substrate preheating, whereas the experiment says deposition parameters are identical except for preheating across APS and cold-spray groups; APS and cold spray cannot have identical process parameters.

The principal thickness prediction is greater than 100 μm, but falsification only requires failure to exceed the ambiguous 15–45 μm baseline by 30%; a result below 100 μm could therefore fail the stated prediction without falsifying it.
